# Helminths

> *Multicellular worms that, with few exceptions, do not multiply inside the human host, so the burden of worms, and the disease, depends on the amount of exposure.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Distinguish roundworms, tapeworms and flukes; relate worm burden to exposure; describe the immune response to helminths |
| Main organisms | *Ascaris lumbricoides* (anchor); hookworms; *Strongyloides stercoralis*, an exception that can multiply in the host |
| Supporting organisms | Tapeworms (*Taenia*); schistosomes; *Toxocara* |
| Later in the course | Gastrointestinal block, public health and travel medicine |
| Scenario questions | Which exposure best explains a described infection |
